[unblureyewear] Fair enough to check. For transparency, we did ask AliExpress manufacturers when sourcing suppliers, and there's a big difference in the quality supplied. Most of them don't have any certifications, some have CE (which only means it was manufactured in China and nothing else). Terrible quality glasses was also one of the reasons we started the site actually.
It kind of sucks because the average person probably can't tell the difference (we have machines to actually test the prescription), but we wanted to sell a product that's actually good.
Also, we're an Australian company so we need to follow the rules/standards…AliExpress doesn't.
We put a lot of care in finding our suppliers and ensured that they are fully compliant with AS/NZS standards ISO 21987.
[Lizard Spock] CE (which only means it was manufactured in China and nothing else)
I thought"CE" stood for for Conformité Européenne, i.e. European Conformity
[unblureyewear] We actually thought that at first too. But if you ask them for the actual proof documentation it's usually the "China Export" certificate rather than the "Conformité Européenne" one. We ensured all our suppliers have proper certification.
[humdingaling] This peaked my interest so did some research
The primary visual contrast between the China Export symbol and the CE (Conformité Européenne) lies in the arrangement of the letters. When it comes to the European CE marking, the initials maintain a consistent and proportional distance between the two characters. In contrast, on the Chinese CE marking, you’ll notice a distinct lack of space between them, with the letters being much closer to each other.
Basically ..the difference is in the spacing between C and E
in short if it comes out of china and they dont make a song and dance about being CE…than its probably safe to assume its C hina E xport
